title: "Those Who Say They Are… and Are Not"
lead: Four times in the seven letters, Jesus quotes a claim and then denies it: those "who call themselves apostles but are not" (2:2), "who say they are Jews and are not" (2:9; 3:9), and Jezebel, "who calls herself a prophet" (2:20). A fifth time he quotes a whole church: "You say, ‘I am rich’... but you don't realize that you are... poor" (3:17). This page asks what the pattern means, where it comes from, and why claims about who you are carried so much weight in John's world.
